From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: AcmeCorp - security & subprocessor follow-up

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great to meet you and the team. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps we discussed around security and third-party risk so your procurement and security teams have what they need:

- SOC 2: You asked whether Redwood has SOC 2 Type II. We do - we maintain SOC 2 Type II for our hosted and dedicated services. I can share the summary/report link and the scope for Acme-specific deployments.
- GDPR / HIPAA: Our platform can be configured for GDPR data residency and we offer HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (BAA) options for customers that need them; we'll confirm the specific controls and encryption in transit/at-rest details for your use case.
- Subprocessors: Per your procurement checklist, please send the subprocessor list (cloud providers, managed services, analytics vendors) you're tracking for third-party mapping. I've noted that Acme is most concerned about: storage of PII, embeddings/hash tokens, and model artifact handling.
- Vendor security questionnaire: We're happy to kick off the standard vendor questionnaire. If you can share the link or Doc (or we can complete your vendor portal), we'll have our security team respond directly.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jordan to send the subprocessor list and any formal questionnaire link (Procurement).
2) We'll provide Redwood's subprocessor CSV and a SOC 2 summary link by EOD next Monday (Mar 29).
3) Our Security lead (Neha) will fill the vendor security questionnaire or coordinate a call if any items need clarification.

Attaching a short checklist for what we usually include (subprocessor name, vendor contact, region, data types processed).

If that sounds right, I'll get the SOC 2 summary and subprocessor export to you next week.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap - that aligns with what we discussed. A couple items from our side:

- SOC 2: We require either a current SOC 2 Type II report or a SOC 2 bridge letter if the report is in process. We're aiming for a final decision by early April; can you confirm when Redwood's most recent Type II report was issued and whether a customer-specific scope can be provided?
- Subprocessors: Attached is the high-level subprocessor list you requested for our mapping (cloud providers + managed services). Note: our security team flags any vendor that stores embeddings or persistent model outputs for additional review.
- Questionnaire: Procurement has a vendor security questionnaire in DocuSign/Portal - I'll route that to you (procurement@acmecorp.com). Alternatively, I can upload the questionnaire to your security portal if that's easier.

For context, our primary concerns are: data residency (US-only for this project), retention of PII/embeddings, and audit log availability for requests to delete data.

Sending the questionnaire now. Let me know if you prefer us to grant portal access or you'll upload responses to our DocuSign link.

Best,
Jordan
Security Programs Lead, AcmeCorp
jmills@acmecorp.com

Hi Jordan - thanks for sending this over and for the clarity on Acme's priorities. Quick updates from Redwood Security:

1) SOC 2: Our latest SOC 2 Type II report was issued 2025-11-15 and covers our hosted API and Dedicated deployment surfaces. We can provide the report summary via a secure link; for procurement we usually share a redacted report or bridge letter if the full report is restricted.

2) Subprocessors: Attached is Redwood's canonical subprocessor list (CSV) - includes cloud providers (AWS - us-east-1 primary, GCP - us-west-2 for backups), monitoring/observability providers, and our managed inference partner for certain Dedicated customers. For this engagement we confirm US-only residency can be enforced via region pinning on your account.

3) Embeddings/PII retention: By default we do not persist model outputs in a way that is accessible for other customers. We keep short-term logs for debugging and provide deletion APIs and audit logs on request. We will mark the questionnaire responses to call out our deletion API endpoints and retention windows.

4) Questionnaire: I'll complete Acme's vendor questionnaire in the portal - please grant us access or forward the DocuSign link. If procurement prefers, I can also upload a filled PDF to the link Jordan included.

We've attached the subprocessor CSV and a SOC2 summary link. If Rishi or Procurement needs a BAA, we have a standard BAA template and can coordinate execution.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
